item.title: UX Improvement Pass + Style Guide for Colorado Mesh's Mesh Client used around the world
item.dc:creator: Colorado Mesh's Mesh Client UX Review
item.description: Howdy OSD Team! Our pet project is now used around the world, in some cases to help bypass censorship and others to help out in emergencies and disasters. It has never had a UX pass by anyone who knows what they are doing. It needs one. We’ve tried to prototype some improvements, but our experiments have all ended in failure. This is because we are lacking a style guide. We do have a codified style, flow, and accessibility features that work for our users. We want to have something more like a standard, and then we can perform a full UI audit against that standard.
item.content:encoded:
Organization: Colorado Mesh's Mesh Client UX Review

Status: searching

Compensation: gratis

Role: UX Review

Howdy OSD Team! Our pet project is now used around the world, in some cases to help bypass censorship and others to help out in emergencies and disasters. It has never had a UX pass by anyone who knows what they are doing. It needs one. We’ve tried to prototype some improvements, but our experiments have all ended in failure. This is because we are lacking a style guide. We do have a codified style, flow, and accessibility features that work for our users. We want to have something more like a standard, and then we can perform a full UI audit against that standard.

Our GPL-3 app is a desktop-only Electron app (with a Rust sidecar) that works on macOS, Linux, and Windows. It allows for the use of Meshtastic, MeshCore, and Reticulum simultaneously and also has built-in support for emergency management and use cases (e.g., Mesh Emergency Communications Protocol as well as TAK server support).

The app uses a dark, dense desktop “engineering dashboard” UX: near-black and slate surfaces, green brand accents, protocol-specific color coding, compact monospace technical text, bordered rounded panels, status indicators, tabs, sidebars, modals, and toasts, with restrained hover/pulse animations. It is built with Electron, React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, and Zustand, enhanced by Motion, Lucide icons, TanStack Virtual, Recharts, Leaflet, xterm, i18next, and emoji-picker-element, with Vitest, Testing Library, and axe supporting its accessibility-focused testing.

We’d like to have someone take a pass at improving the UX and generating a style guide. Once we confirm that the proposed style (via mock-ups) will work on our end, we’d like the designer to generate the full style guide, and we’ll implement. Soliciting user requirements and technical limitations from the developers will be crucial for success.

AI assistance is authorized.

We’re happy to have one person or a self-assembling team that operates independently.

How to Apply:

  • Join the #mesh-client channel on Discord: https://discord.com/invite/NX77SYan3P, then ping "NV0N - Joey".

item.title: Front-end developer (UI) for Corro — an accessibility-first board & card game platform
item.dc:creator: Corro
item.description: Corro is an accessibility-first engine for online board and card games — built so that everyone plays the same game together, whatever their abilities. The name evokes a circle of people holding hands as equals, with no head of the table. Accessibility is the foundation of the codebase, not an afterthought. You can try it live at https://allwelcome.games. I’m the founder, and I’m blind. The engine already treats accessibility as a first-class concern — ARIA live regions for game announcements, full keyboard navigation and focus management, native dialog modals with focus trapping, semantic HTML and server-authoritative announcements. What the front-end needs now is polish: a UI that is as visually refined and pleasant as it is accessible.
item.content:encoded:
Organization: Corro

Status: searching

Compensation: gratis

Role: Front-end development, UI implementation

Corro is an accessibility-first engine for online board and card games — built so that everyone plays the same game together, whatever their abilities. The name evokes a circle of people holding hands as equals, with no head of the table. Accessibility is the foundation of the codebase, not an afterthought. You can try it live at https://allwelcome.games.

I’m the founder, and I’m blind. The engine already treats accessibility as a first-class concern — ARIA live regions for game announcements, full keyboard navigation and focus management, native dialog modals with focus trapping, semantic HTML and server-authoritative announcements. What the front-end needs now is polish: a UI that is as visually refined and pleasant as it is accessible.

What we’re looking for

A front-end developer to improve and beautify Corro’s interface — refining layout, responsiveness and visual detail across the lobby and in-game screens — without breaking the accessibility that is the whole point of the project. You’d work closely with our illustrator/designer to bring the visual layer to life in the browser.

Tech stack

  • Vanilla TypeScript (no bundler), vanilla CSS
  • i18next for localization (English & Spanish today)
  • Backend is .NET 10 / ASP.NET Core / SignalR — but this role is front-end focused

What you’d help with

  • Refining and beautifying the lobby and in-game UI (CSS, layout, responsive/mobile)
  • Integrating new artwork and icons into the interface
  • Keeping everything keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly as the UI evolves
  • Small, well-scoped improvements to focus management, live regions and semantic markup

A good fit if you

  • Are comfortable with modern vanilla TypeScript and CSS (no framework required)
  • Take accessibility seriously — or want to get genuinely good at it
  • Enjoy careful, detail-oriented UI work
  • Are happy contributing to an AGPL-3.0 open-source project

This is a volunteer role. If you want your front-end skills to help build a more inclusive place to play, get in touch.

How to Apply:

  • juanjo@jmontiel.es
  • https://github.com/kastwey/corro

item.title: Illustrator & graphic designer for Corro — an accessibility-first board & card game platform
item.dc:creator: Corro
item.description: Corro is an accessibility-first engine for online board and card games — designed so that everyone plays the same game together, whatever their abilities. The name comes from the image of a circle of people holding hands as equals, with no head of the table. Accessibility isn’t a feature we bolt on; it’s the foundation of the architecture. You can try the live platform at https://allwelcome.games. I’m the founder, and I’m blind. I’ve built the engine so that a blind player and a sighted player can share the exact same match — same board, same cards, same turns. What I can’t do myself is make that shared world beautiful to look at. That’s where you come in.
item.content:encoded:
Organization: Corro

Status: searching

Compensation: gratis

Role: Illustration, game art, graphic design

Corro is an accessibility-first engine for online board and card games — designed so that everyone plays the same game together, whatever their abilities. The name comes from the image of a circle of people holding hands as equals, with no head of the table. Accessibility isn’t a feature we bolt on; it’s the foundation of the architecture. You can try the live platform at https://allwelcome.games.

I’m the founder, and I’m blind. I’ve built the engine so that a blind player and a sighted player can share the exact same match — same board, same cards, same turns. What I can’t do myself is make that shared world beautiful to look at. That’s where you come in.

What we’re looking for

An illustrator / graphic designer to give Corro’s games a warm, cohesive visual identity: illustrating cards, tiles, boards, pieces and other in-game elements, and helping shape a consistent art style across the platform. Your work would be the visual layer of a game that blind and sighted people can finally enjoy side by side.

What you’d help with

  • Illustrations for cards, tiles, boards, tokens and game pieces
  • A coherent visual style and small art guidelines others can follow
  • Icons and visual elements for the game interface
  • Delivering artwork in open, reusable formats (SVG preferred where possible) so it can ship inside Corro’s .corro game packages

A good fit if you

  • Love game art and illustration and want your work to have real social impact
  • Care about (or are curious about) inclusive and accessible design
  • Are happy collaborating in the open on an AGPL-3.0 project
  • Bonus: any experience with high-contrast, colour-blind-friendly or otherwise accessible visual design

This is a volunteer role on an open-source project. If sharing play — rather than gatekeeping it — is something you believe in, I’d love to build this with you.

item.title: We'd like a children's book for TUF!

Forgejo is a self-hosted platform for software development (version tracking and project management).

Dear design community, I’m looking for assistance for my role in the Forgejo user research team. Currently, I’m the only member of that team, and I publicly called for help with my roles recently, because I cannot keep up with the work on my own.

item.title: UX/UI review of AntennaPod player screen (to fit more features)
item.dc:creator: AntennaPod
item.description: AntennaPod is a well-known open-source app for Android to subscribe and listen to podcasts. The podcast space is innovating, and we want to add a whole bunch of functionalities. Many of these features need to be made accessible from the player screen. We need to find a way to do that, while keeping the screen clean and user friendly. What we’ll work on updating/integrating specifically: New: Way to open transcript New: Speaker image + name (based on transcript) New: Way to open podcast comments (ActivityPub replies) + ideally an indicator of number of comments (to encourage to look) New: Display of current chapter title Adapt: Way to access shownotes & chapters Adapt: Chapter navigation Adapt: Sleep timer button New: Sleep timer remaining time indication To consider for the future: bookmark timestamp; value4value streaming & boost (payment functionality) We would love to get a small group (2-3) of experienced UX/UI designers to help us redefine the player screen. We expect this exercise to take about 6 months (about 2 hours per week on average: 1 hour work, 1 hour meeting). AntennaPod core team members will be heavily involved (you’re not left to your own devices).
item.content:encoded:
Organization: AntennaPod

Status: closed

Compensation: gratis

Role: Interaction design, UX study

AntennaPod is a well-known open-source app for Android to subscribe and listen to podcasts. The podcast space is innovating, and we want to add a whole bunch of functionalities. Many of these features need to be made accessible from the player screen. We need to find a way to do that, while keeping the screen clean and user friendly.

What we’ll work on updating/integrating specifically:

  • New: Way to open transcript
  • New: Speaker image + name (based on transcript)
  • New: Way to open podcast comments (ActivityPub replies) + ideally an indicator of number of comments (to encourage to look)
  • New: Display of current chapter title
  • Adapt: Way to access shownotes & chapters
  • Adapt: Chapter navigation
  • Adapt: Sleep timer button
  • New: Sleep timer remaining time indication
  • To consider for the future: bookmark timestamp; value4value streaming & boost (payment functionality)

We would love to get a small group (2-3) of experienced UX/UI designers to help us redefine the player screen. We expect this exercise to take about 6 months (about 2 hours per week on average: 1 hour work, 1 hour meeting). AntennaPod core team members will be heavily involved (you’re not left to your own devices).

How to Apply:

item.title: Looking for Designer for a free software
item.dc:creator: KeyFortress
item.description: I am looking for someone to join my team, i am software developer and at my day job i lead a small team of people, in my spare time i am always trying to contribute to society by creating free software that benefits the people and not the companies around the world. There are no time commitments, we work whenever we have time and the only requirement that i have is someone that shares my passion to make the world a better
item.content:encoded:
Organization: KeyFortress

Status: expired

Compensation: gratis

Role: UI/UX and Logo

I am looking for someone to join my team, i am software developer and at my day job i lead a small team of people, in my spare time i am always trying to contribute to society by creating free software that benefits the people and not the companies around the world.

There are no time commitments, we work whenever we have time and the only requirement that i have is someone that shares my passion to make the world a better

The ideal person for the job would be someone that is well versed with UI/UX, Branding and any design software of your own choice. Since this is not a paid position i am open to people with any type of experience, we are all together in this journey to grow.

Currently, i have two software projects that i am planning to finish this year. Let me tell you more a bout the first one that would be quicker.

The name is KeyFortress and it’s a new authentication application, with support for end to end encryption, and built in protocol for passwordess authentication, it might be a bit early for the adoption on the market, but being first is never a bad thing.

You can read a bit more on the protocol here: https://owasp.org/www-pdf-archive/PLA_OWASP_APPSEC_APAC-2012_Conference_V1.2.9.

I have a working version of the application already, and i plan to release it for Windows, Linux, MacOS, IOS, and Android. So i am looking for a partner that is here for the long run, and i do hope that in the process we manage to establish something bigger together.

Currently only IOS and Android have an MVP, but probably the end of the month there will be MVPs for the 3 desktops as well.

The tech stack that i currently use for those that are interested is:

Flutter/Dart - for both the Desktop and Mobile applications HTMX,Express, Blazor for all web based consumers (Couple of example web pages so we can demonstrate how the login works) A .Net core API that all of the Web pages use to authenticate against

I am also looking for other roles, so if you want to contribute but don’t find yourself fitting these requirements, hit me up, we will figure something out.

How to Apply:

  • Kristifor Milchev <kristiformilchev@outlook.com>
  • https://github.com/KristiforMilchev/KeyFortress
